sql: SELECT "PROJECT NAME", "ADDRESS", "DATE ISSUED"::text AS "DATE ISSUED" FROM "c21106f9-3ef5-4f3a-8604-f992b4db7512" WHERE "PERMIT TYPE"='Comm New Building Permit' AND ("PROJECT NAME" ILIKE '%apart%' OR "PROJECT NAME" ILIKE '%multifamily%' OR "PROJECT NAME" ILIKE '%multi-family%' OR "PROJECT NAME" ILIKE 'AFF -%') UNION ALL SELECT "PROJECT NAME", "ADDRESS", "DATE ISSUED"::text AS "DATE ISSUED" FROM "c22b1ef2-dcf8-4d77-be1a-ee3638092aab" WHERE "PERMIT TYPE"='Comm New Building Permit' AND ("PROJECT NAME" ILIKE '%apart%' OR "PROJECT NAME" ILIKE '%multifamily%' OR "PROJECT NAME" ILIKE '%multi-family%' OR "PROJECT NAME" ILIKE 'AFF -%') LIMIT 1000
live_test: Audited live 2026-09-20 (S5). True totals asked of the endpoint itself: the 2025+ resource holds 143,731 rows with a newest DATE ISSUED of 2026-09-18 (two days old -- the feed is NOT frozen); the 2020-2024 resource holds 368,297 rows ending 2024-12-31. The old recipe returned 156 rows whose newest permit was 2025-11-24, 300 days old, because "PROJECT NAME" ILIKE '%apart%' matched nothing after 2025: counted live, apartment-worded 'Comm New Building Permit' rows appear only between 2025-07 and 2025-12 (54 rows) and are zero in 2026 (0 of 411 commercial new-building permits) and zero in H1 2025. San Antonio instead prefixes its affordable-housing-bond apartment projects 'AFF - ': 116 such commercial new-building rows in 2025 and 83 in 2026 across 14 distinct addresses. Verified against the city's own published 2022-2027 Affordable Housing Bond active-projects list (https://www.sa.gov/files/assets/main/v/10/nhsd/documents/housing-bond-active-projects-list.pdf, dated 2026-04-17): permit 'AFF - 1231 E COMMERCE ST - Central at Commerce' (issued 2026-03-16) = Central at Commerce, 279 units; permits 'AFF - 6210 SUN VALLEY DR / 6415 SW 410 - Heritage Estates at Medina' (issued 2026-06-04) = Heritage Estates at Medina, 86 units -- an 86-unit senior apartment community, independently confirmed by bldup/Zabalist; 'AFF - 5578 TEZEL' / 'AFF - 5590 TEZEL' = Tezel Road Apartments, 78 units. Names and unit counts match.
notes: No units field anywhere in this dataset -- units stay None ('Units: not public yet'), per the plan. The city DOES publish unit counts for every 'AFF - ' project in its Affordable Housing Bond active-projects PDF (Central at Commerce 279, Heritage Estates at Medina 86, Tezel Road Apartments 78, Leon Creek Flats 308, Los Arcos at VIDA 324, ...), but that is a separate PDF source, not this endpoint -- recorded as a finding, not wired in here. Each apartment 'project' shows up as one row per building on the site (e.g. 8 rows for the Orion Apartments' 8 buildings + clubhouse) -- find_upcoming's existing address-based merge_records collapses same-address rows into one project, same as San Marcos, so a much smaller lead count than row count is expected here and is not by itself a fault. UNION ALL required an explicit ::text cast on DATE ISSUED because the two resources' column types don't match (2020-2024 resource stores it differently) -- a plain UNION without the cast fails with a Postgres DatatypeMismatch error, confirmed live. That same type mismatch made the 2020-2024 resource return dates as '2021-09-21 00:00:00' (a space, not a T), which find_upcoming._parse_date could not read: 100 of 154 apartment rows were silently dropped as 'no usable date' and were NOT counted as aged out, so the run's own alarm reported agedOut=0. _parse_date now reads that shape, so those rows are honestly counted as aged out (they are all 2021-2023 and stay out of the leads either way). This dataset has four columns a seller needs that this recipe still drops: 'AREA (SF)', 'DECLARED VALUATION', 'PRIMARY CONTACT' (a real named contact on the permit) and 'PERMIT #'. A new adapter, skills/lead-finder-permits/ckan_sql.py, wraps CKAN's datastore_search_sql {result:{records:[...]}} envelope into the plain-list shape find_upcoming's _fetch_rows already understands from Socrata. Note CKAN's SQL endpoint answers 403 Forbidden for substring() and regexp_replace(); plain comparisons, count, max and GROUP BY are fine. Two rows for 4511 Thousand Oaks carry no address at all (one None, one the literal string 'NULL'), which used to become a lead whose address read 'None'; find_upcoming now drops a permit row with no usable street address and counts it as noAddress. The 'AFF - ' filing code is stripped off the project name via name_strip_pattern; what is left still leads with the street ('6415 SW 410 - Heritage Estates at Medina') and would read better after the wider building-name cleanup task.
